The instruction pipeline

Four stages.
One instruction.

Scroll through a simplified CPU pipeline, from the first memory read to the final register update.

Stage 01 / F

Fetch

Read the next instruction from memory using the program counter.

Stage 02 / D

Decode

Identify the operation and read the registers it needs.

Stage 03 / E

Execute

Carry out the operation, such as adding two values in the arithmetic logic unit.

Stage 04 / W

Write

Store the result in the destination register when the instruction produces one.

Get started

Overlap saves time.

While one instruction decodes, the CPU can fetch the next. Once the pipeline fills, all four stages can work on different instructions in the same clock cycle.

Sequential40 ns
Pipelined16 ns
Speedup2.5×

Five instructions, four stages at 2 ns each, with no stalls or pipeline-register overhead. Sequential execution takes 20 cycles. Pipelined execution takes 8 cycles.
